description: Grouped view of a run's raw_games rows, per appid, across the three sources enrichment actually consumes (steamspy_all, steam_appdetails, steam_reviews). steamspy_appdetails is intentionally absent -- confirmed resolution: tags and per-app SteamSpy detail are sourced from the bulk steamspy_all payload only.
docstring:
Per-appid raw payload groups for one run.

Attributes:
    run_id: The run these payloads belong to.
    steamspy: appid -> the app's SteamSpy bulk record (from source='steamspy_all').
    appdetails: appid -> the app's {"success":..., "data":{...}} Steam appdetails payload (from source='steam_appdetails'). Keys are the candidate appids only (appdetails is never fetched for non-candidates).
    reviews: appid -> the app's review-summary payload (from source='steam_reviews').

An appid present in `steamspy` but absent from `appdetails`/`reviews` means that per-app fetch failed or was never attempted (e.g. the app was excluded by the coarse filter, or its detail fetch failed and only a transport-error stub was persisted).
postconditions: Every key in appdetails and reviews is also a key in steamspy (candidates are always a subset of the full bulk catalog by construction)
Values are the raw parsed JSON dicts exactly as persisted, with no normalization applied yet

edge_cases.input: An appid present in appdetails with payload {'<appid>': {'success': false}}
edge_cases.expected_behavior: retained as-is; normalize_features is responsible for interpreting success=false as a dropped row

edge_cases.input: An appid with no reviews entry at all (fetch never attempted or lost)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: simply absent from the reviews dict; normalize_features must handle a missing key, not assume every appdetails key has a matching reviews key

unit_tests.name: test_bundle_grouping_from_fixture
unit_tests.description: tests/fixtures/raw_bundle_small.json produces a RawBundle whose three dicts have the expected key sets and content.
